text: Marie Curie's notebooks are still radioactive. In 1898, she and Pierre found two new elements: polonium, then radium. Radium glowed in the dark, and she handled it for years with no protection. Today her papers sit in lead-lined boxes in Paris. Radium takes sixteen hundred years to lose half its strength.
